results.title: Kourovka Problem 13.46: coset-free partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that every uncountable abelian group $G$ of finite odd exponent can be written as $G = A_1 \cup A_2$ with $A_1$ and $A_2$ disjoint, so that for every infinite subgroup $H$ of $G$ and every $g \in G$, the coset $gH$ is contained neither in $A_1$ nor in $A_2$. The problem is due to I. V. Protasov.

results.title: Uncountable abelian groups of odd exponent have coset-free partitions
results.caption: Theorem

This answers Kourovka Problem 13.46 in the affirmative.

results.title: Sums of two positive triangular numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a sum of two positive triangular numbers if there are natural numbers $a \ge 1$ and $b \ge 1$ with $2n = a(a+1) + b(b+1)$, that is, $n = \frac{a(a+1)}{2} + \frac{b(b+1)}{2}$.

results.title: Park's theorem on multiplicative functions additive on sums of two triangular numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a multiplicative arithmetic function with values in $\mathbb{C}$ (so $f$ is defined on the natural numbers with $f(0) = 0$) such that $f(a + b) = f(a) + f(b)$ whenever $a$ and $b$ are both sums of two positive triangular numbers. Then either $f(n) = n$ for every natural number $n$, or $f(n) = 0$ for every natural number $n \notin \{1, 3, 5\}$ and $f(3) f(5) = 0$.

results.title: Forward shift of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The forward shift of a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ is the sequence $S x$ with $(S x)_0 = 0$ and $(S x)_{n+1} = x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Backward shift of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For any type $K$, the backward shift of a sequence $x \colon \mathbb{N} \to K$ is the sequence $n \mapsto x_{n+1}$: it drops the coordinate $x_0$ and shifts every other coordinate down by one.

results.title: The forward shift of a square-summable sequence is square-summable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every square-summable sequence $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots)$ in $\mathbb{K}$, the forward-shifted sequence $(0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ is also square-summable, that is, it belongs to $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The backward shift of an $\ell^2$ sequence is in $\ell^2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the backward shift $n \mapsto x_{n+1}$ of the sequence $x$ is square-summable, that is, it lies in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

reading_title.source: The backward shift of an $\ell^2$ sequence is in $\ell^2$

results.title: Forward shift as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The forward shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ sending $x$ to the forward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, to $(0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$, which is again square-summable.

results.title: Backward shift as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward-shift linear map is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $B$ from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$ for all $x$ and all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Coordinates of the forward-shift linear map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the forward-shift linear map applied to $x$ equals the $i$-th term of the forward shift of the sequence $x$, namely $0$ for $i = 0$ and $x_{i-1}$ for $i \ge 1$.

results.title: Coordinates of the backward-shift linear map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the image of $x$ under the backward-shift linear map $B$ is the $i$-th term of the backward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, $(Bx)_i = x_{i+1}$.

results.title: Square sum of the forward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the forward shift $S x = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ of $x$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |(S x)_i|^2 = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|^2$.

results.title: Square sum of the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the backward shift $(x_1, x_2, \dots)$ of $x$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_{i+1}|^2 \le \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|^2$: the left side is a tail of the right side.

results.title: The forward shift linear map preserves norms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the forward shift on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, viewed as a linear map and given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The backward shift linear map does not increase norms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be the backward shift on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, viewed as a linear map and given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then $\|Bx\| \le \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The unilateral shift operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift is the bounded linear operator $S$ on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$ given by $S(x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. It is bounded because $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x$.

results.title: Backward shift
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward shift is the bounded linear operator $B$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$ for all $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Coordinates of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(Sx)_i$ is the $i$-th term of the forward shift of $x$: $(Sx)_0 = 0$ and $(Sx)_{n+1} = x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Coordinates of the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the backward shift $Bx$ is the $i$-th term of the backward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, $(Bx)_i = x_{i+1}$.

results.title: The unilateral shift preserves norms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The unilateral shift preserves distances
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is an isometry: $\|Sx - Sy\| = \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The unilateral shift has operator norm one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then the operator norm of $S$ is $\|S\| = 1$.

results.title: The backward shift has operator norm at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be the backward shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then the operator norm of $B$ satisfies $\|B\| \le 1$.

results.title: Adjoint of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The adjoint of the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the backward shift $B$: $S^* = B$.

results.title: Left inverse of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward shift $B$ is a left inverse of the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$: $BS = I$, where $I$ is the identity operator.

results.title: The unilateral shift is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is injective.

results.title: Coordinates of the unilateral shift after the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$ let $S$ be the unilateral shift, $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$, and $B$ the backward shift, $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(SBx)_i$ is $0$ if $i = 0$ and is $x_i$…

results.title: The unilateral shift composed with the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the unilateral (forward) shift and $B$ the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0$ be the first standard basis vector. Then $S \circ B = 1 - P$, where $P$ is the rank-one operator $P x = \langle e_0, x \rangle e_0 = x_0 e_0$.

results.title: The unilateral shift is not surjective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $S$ is not surjective.

results.title: Geometric sequences with ratio of norm less than one are square-summable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. Then the sequence $(c^i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ lies in $\ell^2$, that is, $\sum_{i} \|c^i\|^2 < \infty$.

results.title: Geometric vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. The geometric vector of $c$ is the sequence $(1, c, c^2, \dots)$, that is $i \mapsto c^i$, regarded as an element of the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences.

results.title: Coordinates of the geometric vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the geometric vector of $c$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is $c^i$.

results.title: The geometric vector is nonzero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. The geometric vector $(1, c, c^2, \dots)$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is nonzero, since its $0$-th coordinate is $1$.

results.title: Backward shift of the geometric vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. Let $v = (1, c, c^2, \dots)$ be the geometric vector of $c$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $B$ be the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Then $Bv = c\,v$.

results.title: The identity on ℓ²(ℕ) has norm at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The operator norm of the identity operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is at most $1$.

results.title: Applying a scalar operator minus an operator on ℓ²(ℕ)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, and let $\mu I$ be the image of $\mu$ under the algebra map from $\mathbb{K}$ into the bounded operators, i.e. $\mu$ times the identity $I$. Then $(\mu I - T)x = \mu x - Tx$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The open unit ball lies in the spectrum of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|\mu\| < 1$ lies in the spectrum of $S$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: The open unit ball lies in the spectrum of the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $B$ be the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|\mu\| < 1$ lies in the spectrum of $B$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.

results.title: Spectrum of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum over $\mathbb{K}$ of the unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the closed unit ball $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : |\mu| \le 1\}$ of $\mathbb{K}$.

results.title: Spectrum of the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum of the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, in the algebra of bounded operators, is the closed unit ball $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : \|\mu\| \le 1\}$: the closed unit disc when $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{C}$ and the interval $[-1, 1]$ when $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Iterated forward shift inserts leading zeroes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Iterating the forward-shift function `n` times inserts `n` zeroes in front of the sequence.

results.title: Iterated backward shift drops leading coordinates

results.title: Pointwise action of a power of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Pointwise action of a power of the backward shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pointwise action of `B ^ n`: it drops the first `n` coordinates.

results.title: Backward shift power is a left inverse of the shift power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `B ^ n` is a left inverse of `S ^ n`: shifting up then down recovers the original sequence.

results.title: Range of a power of the unilateral shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A vector is in the range of `S ^ n` iff its first `n` coordinates vanish.

results.caption: Definition

results.summary: A finitely supported sequence is in `ℓ²`.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The linear extension-by-zero map `(Fin n → 𝕜) →ₗ[𝕜] ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)`.

results.title: Pointwise action of the extension-by-zero map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pointwise action of the extension-by-zero map.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Taking first coordinates after extension by zeroes is the identity.

results.title: Kernel vectors of a backward shift power are zero-extended tuples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A vector in the kernel of `B ^ n` is determined by its first `n` coordinates: extending those coordinates by zeroes recovers it.

results.title: Kernel of the backward shift power as a space of finite tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The kernel of `B ^ n` is linearly equivalent to `Fin n → 𝕜`: a vector in the kernel is exactly its first `n` coordinates.

results.title: Finite-dimensionality of the kernel of a backward shift power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The kernel of `B ^ n` is finite-dimensional.

results.title: Dimension of the kernel of a backward shift power
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Kernel of the first-coordinates map is the range of the shift power

results.title: Dimension of the cokernel of a unilateral shift power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The cokernel of `S ^ n` has dimension `n`: the quotient of `ℓ²` by the range of `S ^ n` is equivalent to `Fin n → 𝕜` via the first `n` coordinates.

results.title: Backward shift power inverts the shift power modulo finite rank
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Shift power inverts the backward shift power modulo finite rank

results.summary: The defect `S ^ n ∘L B ^ n - 1` has finite rank: its range lies in the finite-dimensional kernel of `B ^ n`, since applying `B ^ n` after it gives `0`.

results.title: Acceptable symbols
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $G$ of natural numbers and a symbol $s$ of an encoded grammar over an alphabet $T$, which is either a nonterminal $i \in \mathbb{N}$ or a terminal in $T$, $s$ is acceptable when it is a terminal or a nonterminal that occurs in $G$. The test returns a Boolean.

results.title: Acceptable productions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $G$ of nonterminals (natural numbers), the test accepts an encoded production $(A, \rho)$ when every symbol of $\rho$ is acceptable: a terminal always is, and a nonterminal is when it belongs to $G$. So the production is accepted exactly when every nonterminal occurring in $\rho$ belongs to $G$.

results.title: One round of the generating-nonterminal computation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let a list of productions be given, each a pair of a nonterminal $A \in \mathbb{N}$ and a right-hand side made of nonterminals and terminals, together with a list $G$ of nonterminals. One round returns, in order, the left-hand sides of those productions in whose right-hand side every nonterminal belongs to $G$.

results.title: Generating nonterminals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, start from the empty list of nonterminals and, in each round, replace the current list $G$ by the list of left-hand sides of those productions of $g$ whose right-hand sides contain no nonterminal outside $G$. The generating nonterminals of $g$ are the list obtained after as many rounds as $g$ has productions.

results.title: The emptiness test for context-free grammars

results.title: The generating nonterminals are closed under one more round
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, one more round of the generating-nonterminal computation, applied to the productions of $g$ and the generating nonterminals of $g$, yields only generating nonterminals of $g$: every left-hand side of a production of $g$ whose right-hand side has all its nonterminals among the generating nonterminals of $g$ is itself a generating nonterminal of $g$.

results.title: Pumping bound of an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Letters of generated words occur in the productions

results.title: Pumping lemma for encoded grammars
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Long words make a context-free language infinite
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Context-free pumping down below twice the pumping bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar, let $L$ be the largest of $2$ and the lengths of the right-hand sides of the productions of $g$, let $K$ be the number of distinct left-hand sides of these productions, and let $N = L^{K+1}$ be the pumping bound of $g$. For every word $w$ in the language of $g$ with $|w| \ge N$, there is a word $v$ in the language of $g$ with $N \le |v| < 2N$.

results.title: Correctness of the infiniteness test

results.title: Multi-step evaluation is a congruence in function position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ and $f'$ be terms of type $A \Rightarrow B$ and let $a$ be a term of type $A$, all in the same context. If $f$ evaluates to $f'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then the application $f\,a$ evaluates to $f'\,a$ in zero or more steps.

results.title: Evaluating the argument of a value function is a multi-step congruence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a term of type $A \Rightarrow B$ and let $a$, $a'$ be terms of type $A$, all in the same context. If $f$ is a value and $a$ evaluates to $a'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then the application $f\,a$ evaluates to $f\,a'$ in zero or more steps.

results.title: Evaluation to a value passes through every reduct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the same type in the same context, with $v$ a value. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ and $t$ evaluates to $t'$, each in finitely many call-by-value steps, then $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in finitely many steps.

results.title: Termination of closed terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A closed term $t$ terminates when it evaluates, in finitely many call-by-value steps, to a value.

results.title: Values terminate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every closed term of the simply typed lambda calculus that is a value terminates.

results.title: Termination is closed under backward evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps and $t'$ terminates, then $t$ terminates.

results.title: Termination is closed under forward evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ terminates and $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t'$ terminates.

results.title: Tait reducibility for closed terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Reducibility of a closed term $t$ is defined by recursion on its simple type. At a base type, $t$ is reducible when it terminates. At a function type $A \Rightarrow B$, $t$ is reducible when it terminates and, for every reducible closed term $a$ of type $A$, the application $t\,a$ is reducible.

results.title: Reducible terms terminate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every reducible closed term of the simply typed lambda calculus terminates.

results.title: Reducibility is closed under forward evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ is reducible and $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t'$ is reducible.

results.title: Reducibility is closed under backward evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps and $t'$ is reducible, then $t$ is reducible.

results.title: Reducibility is invariant under evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ evaluates to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t$ is reducible if and only if $t'$ is reducible.

results.title: Reducible substitutions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A substitution $\sigma$ that replaces each variable of a context $\Gamma$ by a closed term of the same type is reducible when $\sigma(x)$ is reducible for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$.

results.title: Substitutions on the empty context are reducible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every substitution from the empty context to closed terms is reducible, since the empty context has no variables.

results.title: Extending a reducible substitution by a reducible term keeps it reducible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution that sends each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a closed term of the same type, and let $a$ be a closed term of type $A$. If $\sigma$ and $a$ are reducible, then so is the substitution on the context $A, \Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $x$ to $\sigma(x)$.

results.title: Fundamental theorem of the reducibility relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, and let $\sigma$ be a reducible substitution sending each variable of $\Gamma$ to a closed term of the same type. Then the closed term obtained by applying $\sigma$ to $t$ is reducible.

results.title: Closed terms are reducible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every closed well-typed term of the simply typed lambda calculus is reducible.

results.title: Termination of the call-by-value simply typed lambda calculus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every closed well-typed term evaluates, in finitely many call-by-value steps, to a value.

results.title: Values reduce only to themselves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $v$ and $t$ be terms of the same type in the same context. If $v$ is a value and $v$ reduces to $t$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $v = t$.

results.title: Uniqueness of the value reached by evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a term in any context. If $t$ reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a value $v$ and also to a value $w$, then $v = w$.

results.title: Normalizing closed terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A closed term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus normalizes when it reduces, in zero or more call-by-value steps, to a term in normal form, that is, a term with no further call-by-value reduction step.

results.title: Normalization and termination coincide
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A closed well-typed term $t$ normalizes, that is, reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form (a term with no further reduction step), if and only if it terminates, that is, reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a value.

results.title: Normalization of closed terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every closed well-typed term normalizes: it reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form.

results.title: Uniqueness of normal forms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a closed term $t$ reduces in zero or more call-by-value steps to a normal form $n$ and also to a normal form $m$, then $n = m$.

results.title: Closed functions evaluate to lambda abstractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every closed term $f$ of a function type $A \Rightarrow B$ there is a term $b$ of type $B$ in the context with a single variable of type $A$ such that $f$ reduces, in zero or more call-by-value steps, to the lambda abstraction with body $b$.

results.title: No closed terms of base type
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the pure, constant-free calculus there is no closed term whose type is a base type.

results.title: Closed terms with the same result
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two closed terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type have the same result when there is a value $v$ such that both $t$ and $u$ reduce to $v$ in zero or more call-by-value steps.

results.title: Reflexivity of having the same result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every closed term has the same result as itself.

results.title: Symmetry of having the same result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If closed terms $t$ and $u$ have the same result, then $u$ and $t$ have the same result.

results.title: Transitivity of having the same result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If closed terms $t$ and $u$ have the same result, and $u$ and a closed term $v$ have the same result, then $t$ and $v$ have the same result.

results.title: Evaluation preserves the result of a closed term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a closed term $t$ reduces to a term $u$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.

results.title: Left expansion preserves having the same result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $u$ be closed terms of the same type. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, and $t'$ and $u$ have the same result, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.

results.title: Right expansion preserves having the same result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$, $u$ and $u'$ be closed terms of the same type. If $u$ reduces to $u'$ in zero or more call-by-value steps, and $t$ and $u'$ have the same result, then $t$ and $u$ have the same result.

results.title: Application preserves having the same result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ and $g$ be closed terms of a function type $A \Rightarrow B$, and let $a$ and $b$ be closed terms of type $A$. If $f$ and $g$ have the same result and $a$ and $b$ have the same result, then the applications $f\,a$ and $g\,b$ have the same result.

results.title: Having the same result is an equivalence relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every simple type $A$, the relation of having the same result is an equivalence relation on the closed terms of type $A$.

results.title: Binary code
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A binary code of length $n$ is a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the vector space of words of length $n$ over the two-element field $\mathbb{F}_2$.

results.title: Dimension of a binary code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dimension of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is its dimension as a vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

results.title: Rate of a binary code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The rate of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is its dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ divided by its length $n$, as a real number; it is $0$ when $n = 0$.

results.title: Minimum distance of a binary code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The distance of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is the smallest Hamming weight (number of nonzero coordinates) of a nonzero codeword of $C$, and is $0$ if $C = \{0\}$.

results.title: Normalised distance of a binary code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The normalised distance of a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is its distance divided by its length $n$, as a real number; it is $0$ when $n = 0$.

results.title: Distance from a word to a binary code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and a word $f \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the distance from $f$ to $C$ is the minimum, over all codewords $c \in C$, of the Hamming distance between $f$ and $c$, that is, the number of coordinates in which $f$ and $c$ differ.

results.title: Normalised distance from a word to a binary code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a binary code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and a word $f \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$, the normalised distance from $f$ to $C$ is the distance from $f$ to $C$ (the Hamming distance from $f$ to a closest codeword) divided by the length $n$, as a nonnegative real number; it is $0$ when $n = 0$.

results.title: Good family of codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(n_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be natural numbers and, for each $i$, let $C_i \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^{n_i}$ be a binary code of length $n_i$. The family $(C_i)$ is good if $n_i \to \infty$ as $i \to \infty$ and there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $i$ both the rate and the normalised distance of $C_i$ are at least $\varepsilon$.

results.title: Subsets with at most $q$ elements
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $q$, this is the collection of all subsets $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $q$ elements.

results.title: Locally testable code
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a binary code, let $q$ be a natural number and let $\kappa \ge 0$ be a real number. A $\kappa$-local tester for $C$ with $q$ queries consists of a probability distribution on the subsets $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at most $q$ elements, together with, for each such $S$, a set $V_S \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^S$ of allowed local views, such that: at least $\kappa$ times…

results.title: Good locally testable codes of every rate below one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho < 1$ there exist a natural number $q$, a real number $\kappa > 0$, lengths $n_i \in \mathbb{N}$ and binary codes $C_i$ of length $n_i$ for $i \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the family $(C_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is good and, for every $i$, the code $C_i$ is $\kappa$-locally testable with $q$ queries and has rate at least $\rho$.
